text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/README
@@
 Collection of sample GEQDSK files
+
+Miller generator
+================
+
+gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py is both an importable module and a command-line
+generator. It requires NumPy and SciPy. Matplotlib is optional, for --plot.
+The implementation plan is MILLER_EQDSK_PLAN.md; all formulas and numerical
+methods are documented in gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex.
+
+From the repository root:
+
+  python3 gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py \
+    gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/miller_tcv.py --output tcv_miller.geqdsk \
+    --nr 257 --nz 257 --plot tcv_miller.png
+
+The Python input defines geometry={...} and a scalar q(R_omp) function. All
+physical parameters belong in that file; the CLI never evaluates a function
+expression. R_omp is outboard midplane MAJOR radius in meters. Required geometry
+keys are R_axis, B_axis (toroidal field), and R_lcfs (outboard LCFS major radius).
+Defaults: Z_axis=0, kappa=1, delta=0, a_shift=0. Lengths are meters and fields
+tesla. The initial convention requires positive B_axis and positive finite q.
+
+Optional R_omp_bounds=(lower,upper) requests coverage of complete flux surfaces
+for a core annulus, SOL-only simulation, or LCFS-crossing simulation. These are
+NOT rectangular R bounds. The equilibrium always includes the axis and LCFS;
+q must be valid all the way from the axis through the physical guard surface.
+Without coverage bounds the LCFS is the outer certified surface. --rz-bounds
+RMIN RMAX ZMIN ZMAX explicitly sets the rectangular grid but does not extend
+the certified physical surfaces. Rectangular corners use the documented smooth
+flux continuation beyond the guard, identified in the JSON summary and plots.
+The default 5-percent guard needs at least three R-Z cells of clearance; coarse
+grids may require --guard-fraction 0.25. The node counts must be odd, 5..999.
+
+The output includes <output>.json, with parameters, input provenance, flux
+values, physical coverage, a conversion table, and numerical residuals. The
+GEQDSK has constant F=R_axis*B_axis and zero pressure/current placeholders. It is
+a synthetic magnetic geometry, not a Grad-Shafranov solution or a wall model.
+No limiter is written. The existing tokamak IWL machinery supplies wall cuts.
+
+Examples miller_d3d.py and miller_tcv.py preserve their corresponding analytic
+regression inputs' surfaces and q profiles. TCV uses the actual shifted r(x)
+endpoint surfaces, not its nominal Rmid bounds. Read it with reflect=false to
+preserve Z_axis. LTX replaces the old rational q profile (pole at R_omp about
+0.688328 m) with a positive exponential profile preserving LCFS q and shear.
+The original script and data file remain available for comparison.
+
+Python API:
+
+  from gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk import (
+      MillerGeometry, MillerEquilibrium, sample_eqdsk, write_eqdsk)
+  geometry = MillerGeometry(R_axis=2, B_axis=1.5, R_lcfs=2.5)
+  equilibrium = MillerEquilibrium(geometry, lambda R_omp: 2)
+  data = sample_eqdsk(equilibrium)
+  write_eqdsk("circle.geqdsk", equilibrium, data)
+  print(equilibrium.coordinates(2.4))  # R_omp, Miller r, psi, rho_psi, q.
+
+Verification:
+
+  python3 -m unittest discover -s gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk -v
+  make -j6 LIBRARY_TARGET=library gyrokinetic
+  make -j6 build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk
+  ./build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk
+
+Use no more than half the available processors for make. To exercise the native
+reader on Python outputs as well, generate files named miller_ltx.geqdsk,
+miller_d3d.geqdsk, and miller_tcv.geqdsk in one directory, then run the same C
+test with GKYL_MILLER_REFERENCE_DIR set to that directory. Native tests always
+construct their own temporary fixtures, so normal unit runs need no Python.
+Both quadratic and cubic reconstructions are checked; full geometry creation
+uses the existing quadratic tokamak path. LaTeX can be checked with:
+
+  pdflatex -halt-on-error -output-directory=/tmp \
+    gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex
+
+Native updater and app API
+=========================
+
+gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.h exposes _inew, _advance, _write, _get_info,
+_psi_from_omp, _omp_from_psi, _surface, and _release. Its qprofile callback takes
+(double R_omp, void *ctx). The native angular quadrature uses periodic
+trapezoidal refinement with an explicit convergence test; radial interpolation
+and the rectangular continuation follow the Python reference. It is a host
+initialization updater, with no CUDA or MPI dependency.
+
+The app accepts geometry.geometry_id=GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER and parameters in
+geometry.miller_grid_info, of type struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inp. In this mode
+app lower[0] and upper[0] are outboard major radii. Initialization resolves the
+mutable input IN PLACE to psi bounds and GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK, before creating
+the configuration grid. Solver callbacks therefore receive the ordinary
+tokamak coordinates (psi, alpha, parallel coordinate). They do not receive the
+old analytic input's (x,y,theta). Use the updater conversions when migrating
+physical profiles. Binormal extents and parallel coordinates use the existing
+tokamak conventions; arbitrary analytic-input callbacks cannot be reused
+without their coordinate transformations.
+
+Generation writes <app-name>-miller.geqdsk unless geometry.efit_info.filepath is
+set. Rank zero writes, collective status handling precedes reading, and the
+file is retained. Generation parameters are recorded in geometry metadata.
+The app selects IWL geometry, disables reflection, and derives R-Z search bounds.
+It supports single-block 2x/3x domains, excluding the coordinate singularity at
+the magnetic axis. Multiblock and language-binding APIs are not provided here.
+
+An LCFS crossing sets has_LCFS and must align with a psi cell face. No requested
+domain surfaces are moved; mismatch beyond GEQDSK serialization precision
+causes initialization to fail. x_LCFS is represented by the matching grid face;
+the wall cutoff uses the serialized boundary flux. Core-only and SOL-only
+domains have no internal split. Set ordinary species BCs: twist-shift for a
+3x core annulus, and the desired open-line BCs for SOL/crossing cases. The app's
+existing mixed-domain machinery handles the core part of a crossing.
+
+The focused regression rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 constructs all three domains and
+advances each by one step. It uses constant profiles and a static zero field
+to isolate geometry/BC initialization. Run in a scratch directory to contain
+its output; MPI partitions the parallel (third configuration) direction:
+
+  make -j6 build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1
+  ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 -s1
+  <MPI-prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 2 \
+    ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 -M -e2 -s1
+
+Check the returned app pointer for NULL after a Miller initialization failure.
 
 Put the geqdsk file you want in this folder and name it 'input.geqdsk' in order to run g0 unit tests with it
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
I'd like to start a new project. My ultimate goal is to have a simple interface in gyrokinetic input files for requesting a Miller tokamak geometry, and provide only the minimum necessary inputs or functions that characterize that magnetic equilibrium. The gyrokinetic app would then generate an .eqdsk file, and run the rest of the simulation using the existing GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK infrastructure.

To that end I'd like to proceed in 3 stages.

# Stage 1: clean up and extend existing python script for generating Miller eqdsk.

Gkeyll has a python script for generating Miller equilibrium,

gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/write_efit_ltx_miller.py

It is presently tailored for the LTX tokamak. I'd like to create a new python script or module (name it gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py) based on this, but such that it works for any tokamak (size, magnetic field, safety factor, shear, etc). For example, I'd like to test it by generating eqdsk files for simulations like gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_d3d_iwl_3x2v_p1.c and gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_tcv_iwl_adapt_source_3x2v_p1.c also. I'd also like its geometry functions to be consistent with the latest version in, for example, gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_tcv_iwl_adapt_source_3x2v_p1.c.

# Stage 2: create a C version of gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py

In this stage translate gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py into an updater to be located in gyrokinetic/zero/ and implement unit tests for it, named gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.

# Stage 3: Plug gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk into gyrokinetic app and provide new Miller API for input files.
In this stage we'll add a new enum gkyl_geometry_id option, say GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER, for which the user's input file will provide a minimum set of parameters and functions (in a sub struct member of gkyl_gk_geometry_inp like struct gkyl_miller_geo_grid_inp miller_grid_info). The gyrokinetic app will then call gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk before initializing the geometry (around line 351 of gyrokinetic/apps/gyrokinetic.c), switch the geometry type to GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK and perform the simulation as if this was a GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK with a numerical magnetic equilibrium.

One detail is that for GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK simulations the input file has input grid coordinate extents, specifically for the first dimension psi, which depend on knowledge of the eqdsk file (so that the user can pick the lower and upper psi). In this workflow it is perhaps not possible to pick psi a priori, so either: A) the user has to run the initialization once just to generate the eqdsk, examine it, pick psi bounds, and run the input file again, or B) the user provides the lower and upper normalized psi (i.e. rho = sqrt((psi - psi_axis)/(psi_sep - psi_axis)) assuming psi increasing outwards), and the app computes the psi bounds after the eqdsk is generated, or C) some other alternative I haven't thought of.

Please evaluate this project and create a plan for it.

Write a comprehensive plan, with details for stage 1 and less detail for stages 2 and 3 for now.

One change I'd like to make to stage 1: for the CLI to gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py, it should take a file which has definitions of the q function in it, rather than expecting the user to type the function out on the command line.

I'd like to discuss 4 things that may modify the plan:


A) I may use this infrastructure to run a simulation with a domain away from both the axis AND the LCFS, or alternatively, for an SOL-only simulation outside the LCFS, or a simulation that has a portion inside and a portion outside the LCFS (like rt_gk_tcv_iwl_adapt_source_3x2v_p1). It's ok to expect the user to know and provide R_lcfs in all cases. Please keep that in mind in the plan.

B) Add to the plan to generate a LaTeX (.tex) file documenting all the formulas and numerical methods used by gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py.

C) You said "For shifted cases, distinguish bounds expressed in actual (R_{\rm omp}) from the existing input files’ linear computational-radius mapping." What exactly are "shifted cases"?

D) What is the expected R_omp_bounds input, and what is that for? especially considering that the deliverable in stage 1 is an eqdsk that defines psi on the R-Z plane (where R is the major radius), not just at a range of minor radius.
ok, please write let me see the final plan and write it to an .md file
Implement the plan.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/README
@@
 Collection of sample GEQDSK files
+
+Miller generator
+================
+
+gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py is both an importable module and a command-line
+generator. It requires NumPy and SciPy. Matplotlib is optional, for --plot.
+The implementation plan is MILLER_EQDSK_PLAN.md; all formulas and numerical
+methods are documented in gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex.
+
+From the repository root:
+
+  python3 gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py \
+    gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/miller_tcv.py --output tcv_miller.geqdsk \
+    --nr 257 --nz 257 --plot tcv_miller.png
+
+The Python input defines geometry={...} and a scalar q(R_omp) function. All
+physical parameters belong in that file; the CLI never evaluates a function
+expression. R_omp is outboard midplane MAJOR radius in meters. Required geometry
+keys are R_axis, B_axis (toroidal field), and R_lcfs (outboard LCFS major radius).
+Defaults: Z_axis=0, kappa=1, delta=0, a_shift=0. Lengths are meters and fields
+tesla. The initial convention requires positive B_axis and positive finite q.
+
+Optional R_omp_bounds=(lower,upper) requests coverage of complete flux surfaces
+for a core annulus, SOL-only simulation, or LCFS-crossing simulation. These are
+NOT rectangular R bounds. The equilibrium always includes the axis and LCFS;
+q must be valid all the way from the axis through the physical guard surface.
+Without coverage bounds the LCFS is the outer certified surface. --rz-bounds
+RMIN RMAX ZMIN ZMAX explicitly sets the rectangular grid but does not extend
+the certified physical surfaces. Rectangular corners use the documented smooth
+flux continuation beyond the guard, identified in the JSON summary and plots.
+The default 5-percent guard needs at least three R-Z cells of clearance; coarse
+grids may require --guard-fraction 0.25. The node counts must be odd, 5..999.
+
+The output includes <output>.json, with parameters, input provenance, flux
+values, physical coverage, a conversion table, and numerical residuals. The
+GEQDSK has constant F=R_axis*B_axis and zero pressure/current placeholders. It is
+a synthetic magnetic geometry, not a Grad-Shafranov solution or a wall model.
+No limiter is written. The existing tokamak IWL machinery supplies wall cuts.
+
+Examples miller_d3d.py and miller_tcv.py preserve their corresponding analytic
+regression inputs' surfaces and q profiles. TCV uses the actual shifted r(x)
+endpoint surfaces, not its nominal Rmid bounds. Read it with reflect=false to
+preserve Z_axis. LTX replaces the old rational q profile (pole at R_omp about
+0.688328 m) with a positive exponential profile preserving LCFS q and shear.
+The original script and data file remain available for comparison.
+
+Python API:
+
+  from gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk import (
+      MillerGeometry, MillerEquilibrium, sample_eqdsk, write_eqdsk)
+  geometry = MillerGeometry(R_axis=2, B_axis=1.5, R_lcfs=2.5)
+  equilibrium = MillerEquilibrium(geometry, lambda R_omp: 2)
+  data = sample_eqdsk(equilibrium)
+  write_eqdsk("circle.geqdsk", equilibrium, data)
+  print(equilibrium.coordinates(2.4))  # R_omp, Miller r, psi, rho_psi, q.
+
+Verification:
+
+  python3 -m unittest discover -s gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk -v
+  make -j6 LIBRARY_TARGET=library gyrokinetic
+  make -j6 build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk
+  ./build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk
+
+Use no more than half the available processors for make. To exercise the native
+reader on Python outputs as well, generate files named miller_ltx.geqdsk,
+miller_d3d.geqdsk, and miller_tcv.geqdsk in one directory, then run the same C
+test with GKYL_MILLER_REFERENCE_DIR set to that directory. Native tests always
+construct their own temporary fixtures, so normal unit runs need no Python.
+Both quadratic and cubic reconstructions are checked; full geometry creation
+uses the existing quadratic tokamak path. LaTeX can be checked with:
+
+  pdflatex -halt-on-error -output-directory=/tmp \
+    gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex
+
+Native updater and app API
+=========================
+
+gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.h exposes _inew, _advance, _write, _get_info,
+_psi_from_omp, _omp_from_psi, _surface, and _release. Its qprofile callback takes
+(double R_omp, void *ctx). The native angular quadrature uses periodic
+trapezoidal refinement with an explicit convergence test; radial interpolation
+and the rectangular continuation follow the Python reference. It is a host
+initialization updater, with no CUDA or MPI dependency.
+
+The app accepts geometry.geometry_id=GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER and parameters in
+geometry.miller_grid_info, of type struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inp. In this mode
+app lower[0] and upper[0] are outboard major radii. Initialization resolves the
+mutable input IN PLACE to psi bounds and GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK, before creating
+the configuration grid. Solver callbacks therefore receive the ordinary
+tokamak coordinates (psi, alpha, parallel coordinate). They do not receive the
+old analytic input's (x,y,theta). Use the updater conversions when migrating
+physical profiles. Binormal extents and parallel coordinates use the existing
+tokamak conventions; arbitrary analytic-input callbacks cannot be reused
+without their coordinate transformations.
+
+Generation writes <app-name>-miller.geqdsk unless geometry.efit_info.filepath is
+set. Rank zero writes, collective status handling precedes reading, and the
+file is retained. Generation parameters are recorded in geometry metadata.
+The app selects IWL geometry, disables reflection, and derives R-Z search bounds.
+It supports single-block 2x/3x domains, excluding the coordinate singularity at
+the magnetic axis. Multiblock and language-binding APIs are not provided here.
+
+An LCFS crossing sets has_LCFS and must align with a psi cell face. No requested
+domain surfaces are moved; mismatch beyond GEQDSK serialization precision
+causes initialization to fail. x_LCFS is represented by the matching grid face;
+the wall cutoff uses the serialized boundary flux. Core-only and SOL-only
+domains have no internal split. Set ordinary species BCs: twist-shift for a
+3x core annulus, and the desired open-line BCs for SOL/crossing cases. The app's
+existing mixed-domain machinery handles the core part of a crossing.
+
+The focused regression rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 constructs all three domains and
+advances each by one step. It uses constant profiles and a static zero field
+to isolate geometry/BC initialization. Run in a scratch directory to contain
+its output; MPI partitions the parallel (third configuration) direction:
+
+  make -j6 build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1
+  ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 -s1
+  <MPI-prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 2 \
+    ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 -M -e2 -s1
+
+Check the returned app pointer for NULL after a Miller initialization failure.
 
 Put the geqdsk file you want in this folder and name it 'input.geqdsk' in order to run g0 unit tests with it
*** End Patch"));

I'd like to start a new project. My ultimate goal is to have a simple interface in gyrokinetic input files for requesting a Miller tokamak geometry, and provide only the minimum necessary inputs or functions that characterize that magnetic equilibrium. The gyrokinetic app would then generate an .eqdsk file, and run the rest of the simulation using the existing GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK infrastructure.

To that end I'd like to proceed in 3 stages.

# Stage 1: clean up and extend existing python script for generating Miller eqdsk.

Gkeyll has a python script for generating Miller equilibrium,

gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/write_efit_ltx_miller.py

It is presently tailored for the LTX tokamak. I'd like to create a new python script or module (name it gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py) based on this, but such that it works for any tokamak (size, magnetic field, safety factor, shear, etc). For example, I'd like to test it by generating eqdsk files for simulations like gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_d3d_iwl_3x2v_p1.c and gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_tcv_iwl_adapt_source_3x2v_p1.c also. I'd also like its geometry functions to be consistent with the latest version in, for example, gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_tcv_iwl_adapt_source_3x2v_p1.c.

# Stage 2: create a C version of gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py

In this stage translate gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py into an updater to be located in gyrokinetic/zero/ and implement unit tests for it, named gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.

# Stage 3: Plug gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk into gyrokinetic app and provide new Miller API for input files.
In this stage we'll add a new enum gkyl_geometry_id option, say GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER, for which the user's input file will provide a minimum set of parameters and functions (in a sub struct member of gkyl_gk_geometry_inp like struct gkyl_miller_geo_grid_inp miller_grid_info). The gyrokinetic app will then call gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk before initializing the geometry (around line 351 of gyrokinetic/apps/gyrokinetic.c), switch the geometry type to GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK and perform the simulation as if this was a GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK with a numerical magnetic equilibrium.

One detail is that for GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK simulations the input file has input grid coordinate extents, specifically for the first dimension psi, which depend on knowledge of the eqdsk file (so that the user can pick the lower and upper psi). In this workflow it is perhaps not possible to pick psi a priori, so either: A) the user has to run the initialization once just to generate the eqdsk, examine it, pick psi bounds, and run the input file again, or B) the user provides the lower and upper normalized psi (i.e. rho = sqrt((psi - psi_axis)/(psi_sep - psi_axis)) assuming psi increasing outwards), and the app computes the psi bounds after the eqdsk is generated, or C) some other alternative I haven't thought of.

Please evaluate this project and create a plan for it.

Write a comprehensive plan, with details for stage 1 and less detail for stages 2 and 3 for now.

One change I'd like to make to stage 1: for the CLI to gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py, it should take a file which has definitions of the q function in it, rather than expecting the user to type the function out on the command line.

I'd like to discuss 4 things that may modify the plan:


A) I may use this infrastructure to run a simulation with a domain away from both the axis AND the LCFS, or alternatively, for an SOL-only simulation outside the LCFS, or a simulation that has a portion inside and a portion outside the LCFS (like rt_gk_tcv_iwl_adapt_source_3x2v_p1). It's ok to expect the user to know and provide R_lcfs in all cases. Please keep that in mind in the plan.

B) Add to the plan to generate a LaTeX (.tex) file documenting all the formulas and numerical methods used by gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py.

C) You said "For shifted cases, distinguish bounds expressed in actual (R_{\rm omp}) from the existing input files’ linear computational-radius mapping." What exactly are "shifted cases"?

D) What is the expected R_omp_bounds input, and what is that for? especially considering that the deliverable in stage 1 is an eqdsk that defines psi on the R-Z plane (where R is the major radius), not just at a range of minor radius.
ok, please write let me see the final plan and write it to an .md file

#pragma once

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>

typedef struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk;

struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inp {
  double r_axis, z_axis, b_axis, r_lcfs; // SI units; r_lcfs is outboard major radius.
  double kappa, delta, a_shift; // Zero kappa selects 1; other zeros are physical defaults.
  double (*qprofile)(double r_omp, void *ctx); // Positive q, argument is major radius [m].
  void *qctx;
  bool has_omp_bounds;
  double omp_bounds[2]; // Optional requested simulation surfaces, as major radii [m].
  int nr, nz; // Odd R-Z node counts, default 257.
  double rtol, guard_fraction; // Defaults 1e-10 and 0.05.
  bool has_rz_bounds;
  double rz_bounds[4]; // Rmin, Rmax, Zmin, Zmax [m].
};

struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_info {
  double psi_axis, psi_boundary, psi_guard;
  double r_lcfs, r_required, r_guard; // Miller minor radii [m].
  double rz_bounds[4];
  double radial_error, clearance_cells;
  int radial_nodes, nr, nz;
};

/** Construct the host generator and radial flux table. Return NULL on failure.
 * @param inp Physical and numerical inputs; callback context must outlive the generator.
 * @param error Error buffer, or NULL.
 * @param error_size Size of error buffer.
 */
gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inew(
  const struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inp *inp, char *error, size_t error_size
);

/** Sample and validate the rectangular mesh, using storage allocated at construction.
 * @param up Generator.
 * @param error Error buffer, or NULL.
 * @param error_size Size of error buffer.
 * @return True on success.
 */
bool gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_advance(gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *up, char *error, size_t error_size);

/** Write a previously sampled GEQDSK atomically in its destination directory.
 * @param up Generator after a successful advance.
 * @param filename Destination path.
 * @param error Error buffer, or NULL.
 * @param error_size Size of error buffer.
 * @return True on success.
 */
bool gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_write(
  const gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *up, const char *filename, char *error, size_t error_size
);

/** Get generator metadata. The returned pointer is owned by up. */
const struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_info *gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_get_info(
  const gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *up
);

/** Evaluate flux at a physical outboard midplane major radius; return NaN outside the guard. */
double gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_psi_from_omp(const gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *up, double r_omp);

/** Invert physical flux to outboard midplane major radius; return NaN outside physical coverage. */
double gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_omp_from_psi(const gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *up, double psi);

/** Evaluate the Miller surface at minor radius r and angle theta, returning R,Z [m]. */
void gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_surface(
  const gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *up, double r, double theta, double rz[2]
);

/** Release a generator and all its host storage; NULL is accepted. */
void gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_release(gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk *up);
\begin{equation}
v=(Z-\Za)/\kappa,\qquad u=r\cos\theta,\qquad
r=\sqrt{u^2+v^2},\qquad \beta=\eta v/r.
\end{equation}
The scalar equation is
\begin{equation}
R=\Ra-\frac{A(u^2+v^2)}{2\Ra}+u\cos\beta-v\sin\beta.
\end{equation}
At the origin the ratio $v/r$ is defined as zero. For $r>0$,
\begin{equation}
\beta_u=-\eta vu/r^3,\qquad
R_u=\cos\beta-Au/\Ra-(u\sin\beta+v\cos\beta)\beta_u.
\end{equation}
Symmetric brackets start at $u=\pm r_g$ and expand by a factor of 1.5 as
needed, at most 12 times. The derivative is checked at 65 locations across
each bracket; a nonpositive derivative rejects a folded branch. Fifty
vectorized bisections solve the equation. Recover $\theta=\operatorname{atan2}(v,u)$
and verify the forward residual is at most $10^{-11}\Ra$.
No scattered interpolation or nearest-point fill is used.

\section{Coverage and rectangular continuation}
The outer required radius is $\max(a,r_{\rm requested,hi})$, or $a$ if bounds
are omitted. The physical guard is $r_g=(1+f)r_{\rm required}$, with $f=0.05$
by default. Automatic rectangular bounds enclose the guard contour with
two percent of its horizontal/vertical span added on each side. Explicit
bounds must contain the axis and have positive minimum major radius.

For $s>s_g=r_g^2$ continue the flux as
\begin{equation}
\psi(s)=\psi(s_g)+g(s_g)(s-s_g).
\end{equation}
This matches flux and its first radial derivative and stays increasing.
It supplies numerical background at rectangular corners; it does not certify
physical flux surfaces outside the guard or require q quadrature there.
The analytic coordinate inverse must remain valid at background points.

Measure distance in units of R and Z mesh spacings. Sampled LCFS and outer
required contours must be at least three cells from the guard and box edges.
Guard distances use a nearest-neighbor tree on 4097 guard points. Insufficient
clearance fails with instructions to refine the mesh or enlarge the guard/box.
All fields, certified bounds, background-node counts, and numerical settings
are recorded in the JSON companion. Optional coverage endpoints are reported
in all four radial coordinates.

\section{GEQDSK serialization}
The header uses a deterministic 48-character label followed by three I4
integers. Arrays use five E16.9 values per line; a partially filled final line
is terminated before the next array. Odd node counts from 5 to 999 are accepted.
The flux array has Z as its outer index and R as its inner (fastest) index.
The four one-dimensional profiles are $F$, zero pressure, zero $FF'$, and
zero pressure derivative. QPSI is evaluated at uniform flux nodes between zero
and $\psi_b$ by inverting the physical radial table. A 257-point closed LCFS
polyline is written as alternating $(R,Z)$ pairs. LIMITR is zero. A temporary
file in the output directory is closed successfully before replacing the
destination. JSON records input provenance and the conventions above.

\section{Examples and verification}
The DIII-D and TCV examples retain the source input's q polynomials, field
normalization, and shaping. TCV's input coordinate is linear in Miller radius;
its exact surfaces have outboard endpoints approximately 1.051359 and
1.155593 m. These differ from its nominal outboard bounds. TCV must be read
with reflection disabled to preserve its vertical offset.

The original LTX rational q has a pole at about 0.688328 m, inside its old
sampled range. The replacement is
\begin{equation}
q(r)=q_a\exp\left[\frac{\hat s_a}{2}\left(\frac{r^2}{a^2}-1\right)\right].
\end{equation}
It preserves $q(a)=q_a$, $[r q'/q]_{a}=\hat s_a$, positivity, and $q'(0)=0$.

For circular, unshifted, constant-q surfaces the independent reference is
\begin{equation}
\psi(r)=\frac{F}{q}\left[\Ra-\sqrt{\Ra^2-r^2}\right]
=\frac{F}{q}\frac{r^2}{\Ra+\sqrt{\Ra^2-r^2}}.
\end{equation}
Tests compare this flux and its inverse to normalized tolerance $10^{-8}$,
check analytic derivatives by finite differences, and read output with an
independent fixed-width parser and Gkeyll's EFIT reader. Rectangular refinement
uses 65, 129, and 257 nodes with sufficient guards. An independent tensor cubic
interpolant reconstructs $\nabla\psi$, $B_p$, and $B$. Contour safety factor is
checked using
\begin{equation}
q=\frac{F}{2\pi}\oint\frac{dl}{R^2B_p}.
\end{equation}
The target relative field and q error on the device simulation regions is
$10^{-3}$. Physical contours are compared before coordinate-dependent metrics.
Failure tests include invalid profiles, folds, inadequate coverage, malformed
inputs, and the original LTX pole. Run the documented tests to obtain current
results; no turbulence simulation is needed for this generator validation.

\begin{equation}
v=(Z-\Za)/\kappa,\qquad u=r\cos\theta,\qquad
r=\sqrt{u^2+v^2},\qquad \beta=\eta v/r.
\end{equation}
The scalar equation is
\begin{equation}
R=\Ra-\frac{A(u^2+v^2)}{2\Ra}+u\cos\beta-v\sin\beta.
\end{equation}
At the origin the ratio $v/r$ is defined as zero. For $r>0$,
\begin{equation}
\beta_u=-\eta vu/r^3,\qquad
R_u=\cos\beta-Au/\Ra-(u\sin\beta+v\cos\beta)\beta_u.
\end{equation}
Symmetric brackets start at $u=\pm r_g$ and expand by a factor of 1.5 as
needed, at most 12 times. The derivative is checked at 65 locations across
each bracket; a nonpositive derivative rejects a folded branch. Fifty
vectorized bisections solve the equation. Recover $\theta=\operatorname{atan2}(v,u)$
and verify the forward residual is at most $10^{-11}\Ra$.
No scattered interpolation or nearest-point fill is used.

\section{Coverage and rectangular continuation}
The outer required radius is $\max(a,r_{\rm requested,hi})$, or $a$ if bounds
are omitted. The physical guard is $r_g=(1+f)r_{\rm required}$, with $f=0.05$
by default. Automatic rectangular bounds enclose the guard contour with
two percent of its horizontal/vertical span added on each side. Explicit
bounds must contain the axis and have positive minimum major radius.

For $s>s_g=r_g^2$ continue the flux as
\begin{equation}
\psi(s)=\psi(s_g)+g(s_g)(s-s_g).
\end{equation}
This matches flux and its first radial derivative and stays increasing.
It supplies numerical background at rectangular corners; it does not certify
physical flux surfaces outside the guard or require q quadrature there.
The analytic coordinate inverse must remain valid at background points.

Measure distance in units of R and Z mesh spacings. Sampled LCFS and outer
required contours must be at least three cells from the guard and box edges.
Guard distances use a nearest-neighbor tree on 4097 guard points. Insufficient
clearance fails with instructions to refine the mesh or enlarge the guard/box.
All fields, certified bounds, background-node counts, and numerical settings
are recorded in the JSON companion. Optional coverage endpoints are reported
in all four radial coordinates.

\section{GEQDSK serialization}
The header uses a deterministic 48-character label followed by three I4
integers. Arrays use five E16.9 values per line; a partially filled final line
is terminated before the next array. Odd node counts from 5 to 999 are accepted.
The flux array has Z as its outer index and R as its inner (fastest) index.
The four one-dimensional profiles are $F$, zero pressure, zero $FF'$, and
zero pressure derivative. QPSI is evaluated at uniform flux nodes between zero
and $\psi_b$ by inverting the physical radial table. A 257-point closed LCFS
polyline is written as alternating $(R,Z)$ pairs. LIMITR is zero. A temporary
file in the output directory is closed successfully before replacing the
destination. JSON records input provenance and the conventions above.

\section{Examples and verification}
The DIII-D and TCV examples retain the source input's q polynomials, field
normalization, and shaping. TCV's input coordinate is linear in Miller radius;
its exact surfaces have outboard endpoints approximately 1.051359 and
1.155593 m. These differ from its nominal outboard bounds. TCV must be read
with reflection disabled to preserve its vertical offset.

The original LTX rational q has a pole at about 0.688328 m, inside its old
sampled range. The replacement is
\begin{equation}
q(r)=q_a\exp\left[\frac{\hat s_a}{2}\left(\frac{r^2}{a^2}-1\right)\right].
\end{equation}
It preserves $q(a)=q_a$, $[r q'/q]_{a}=\hat s_a$, positivity, and $q'(0)=0$.

For circular, unshifted, constant-q surfaces the independent reference is
\begin{equation}
\psi(r)=\frac{F}{q}\left[\Ra-\sqrt{\Ra^2-r^2}\right]
=\frac{F}{q}\frac{r^2}{\Ra+\sqrt{\Ra^2-r^2}}.
\end{equation}
Tests compare this flux and its inverse to normalized tolerance $10^{-8}$,
check analytic derivatives by finite differences, and read output with an
independent fixed-width parser and Gkeyll's EFIT reader. Rectangular refinement
uses 65, 129, and 257 nodes with sufficient guards. An independent tensor cubic
interpolant reconstructs $\nabla\psi$, $B_p$, and $B$. Contour safety factor is
checked using
\begin{equation}
q=\frac{F}{2\pi}\oint\frac{dl}{R^2B_p}.
\end{equation}
The target relative field and q error on the device simulation regions is
$10^{-3}$. Physical contours are compared before coordinate-dependent metrics.
Failure tests include invalid profiles, folds, inadequate coverage, malformed
inputs, and the original LTX pole. Run the documented tests to obtain current
results; no turbulence simulation is needed for this generator validation.

The scalar equation is
\begin{equation}

At the origin the ratio $v/r$ is defined as zero. For $r>0$,

vectorized bisections solve the equation. Recover $\theta=\operatorname{atan2}(v,u)$
and verify the forward residual is at most $10^{-11}\Ra$.
No scattered interpolation or nearest-point fill is used.

The outer required radius is $\max(a,r_{\rm requested,hi})$, or $a$ if bounds
are omitted. The physical guard is $r_g=(1+f)r_{\rm required}$, with $f=0.05$
by default. Automatic rectangular bounds enclose the guard contour with
two percent of its horizontal/vertical span added on each side. Explicit
bounds must contain the axis and have positive minimum major radius.

For $s>s_g=r_g^2$ continue the flux as
\begin{equation}

\end{equation}
This matches flux and its first radial derivative and stays increasing.
It supplies numerical background at rectangular corners; it does not certify
physical flux surfaces outside the guard or require q quadrature there.

integers. Arrays use five E16.9 values per line; a partially filled final line

The flux array has Z as its outer index and R as its inner (fastest) index.
The four one-dimensional profiles are $F$, zero pressure, zero $FF'$, and

Native updater and app API
=========================

gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.h exposes _inew, _advance, _write, _get_info,
_psi_from_omp, _omp_from_psi, _surface, and _release. Its qprofile callback takes
(double R_omp, void *ctx). The native angular quadrature uses periodic
trapezoidal refinement with an explicit convergence test; radial interpolation
and the rectangular continuation follow the Python reference. It is a host
initialization updater, with no CUDA or MPI dependency.

The app accepts geometry.geometry_id=GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER and parameters in
geometry.miller_grid_info, of type struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inp. In this mode
app lower[0] and upper[0] are outboard major radii. Initialization resolves the
mutable input IN PLACE to psi bounds and GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK, before creating
the configuration grid. Solver callbacks therefore receive the ordinary
tokamak coordinates (psi, alpha, parallel coordinate). They do not receive the
old analytic input's (x,y,theta). Use the updater conversions when migrating
physical profiles. Binormal extents and parallel coordinates use the existing
tokamak conventions; arbitrary analytic-input callbacks cannot be reused
without their coordinate transformations.

Generation writes <app-name>-miller.geqdsk unless geometry.efit_info.filepath is
set. Rank zero writes, collective status handling precedes reading, and the
file is retained. Generation parameters are recorded in geometry metadata.
The app selects IWL geometry, disables reflection, and derives R-Z search bounds.
It supports single-block 2x/3x domains, excluding the coordinate singularity at
the magnetic axis. Multiblock and language-binding APIs are not provided here.

An LCFS crossing sets has_LCFS and must align with a psi cell face. No requested
domain surfaces are moved; mismatch beyond GEQDSK serialization precision
causes initialization to fail. x_LCFS is represented by the matching grid face;
the wall cutoff uses the serialized boundary flux. Core-only and SOL-only
domains have no internal split. Set ordinary species BCs: twist-shift for a
3x core annulus, and the desired open-line BCs for SOL/crossing cases. The app's
existing mixed-domain machinery handles the core part of a crossing.

The focused regression rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 constructs all three domains and
advances each by one step. It uses constant profiles and a static zero field
to isolate geometry/BC initialization. Run in a scratch directory to contain
its output; MPI partitions the parallel (third configuration) direction:

  ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 -s1

Generation writes <app-name>-miller.geqdsk unless geometry.efit_info.filepath is
set. Rank zero writes, collective status handling precedes reading, and the
file is retained. Generation parameters are recorded in geometry metadata.
The app selects IWL geometry, disables reflection, and derives R-Z search bounds.
It supports single-block 2x/3x domains, excluding the coordinate singularity at
the magnetic axis. Multiblock and language-binding APIs are not provided here.

An LCFS crossing sets has_LCFS and must align with a psi cell face. No requested
domain surfaces are moved; mismatch beyond GEQDSK serialization precision
causes initialization to fail. x_LCFS is represented by the matching grid face;
the wall cutoff uses the serialized boundary flux. Core-only and SOL-only
domains have no internal split. Set ordinary species BCs: twist-shift for a
3x core annulus, and the desired open-line BCs for SOL/crossing cases. The app's
existing mixed-domain machinery handles the core part of a crossing.

advances each by one step. It uses constant profiles and a static zero field
to isolate geometry/BC initialization. Run in a scratch directory to contain

# Miller GEQDSK generation and gyrokinetic app integration

## Objectives and agreed design

Implement three stages in order: a validated Python generator, a native C
updater, and integration into the gyrokinetic app. Stage 1 is specified in
detail; the exact C and app interfaces are finalized after its validation.

The initial model matches the existing DIII-D and TCV analytic inputs: constant
elongation and triangularity, a constant vertical offset, a quadratic Shafranov
shift, and a user-supplied safety-factor function. One Python input file contains
all physical parameters and `q`; CLI options control output and numerics.

Support a core annulus away from axis and LCFS, an SOL-only domain, and a domain
crossing the LCFS. Require `R_lcfs` in every case. The equilibrium extends from
the axis through the LCFS and any requested outer surfaces, independently of
the simulation's inner boundary.

The result is a synthetic magnetic geometry, not a general Grad–Shafranov
solution. Initial topology support is core and inner wall limited; the Miller
surface model does not create diverted X-points.

## Stage 1: Python module

### Deliverables and inputs

- Add `gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py` alongside the existing EQDSK scripts, as both
  an importable module and a CLI. Importing must not write files or show plots.
- Add LTX, DIII-D, and TCV Python inputs, focused Python tests, and a focused C
  compatibility test using the existing EFIT and tokamak geometry readers.
- Add `gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex` documenting all implemented formulas and
  numerical methods; update the EQDSK README with reproducible commands.
- Preserve the original LTX script and equilibrium for comparison.
- Use NumPy/SciPy and standard-library input loading, writing, and tests.
  Matplotlib is needed only for optional saved plots.

The input defines `geometry`, with required `R_axis`, `B_axis`, and `R_lcfs`
(outboard midplane LCFS major radius). Defaults: `Z_axis=0`, `kappa=1`, `delta=0`,
and `a_shift=0`. Define `q(R_omp)` accepting a scalar outboard midplane major
radius in meters. Helpers, constants, and imports are permitted. Provide a
documented conversion helper for profiles written in Miller minor radius.

Optional `R_omp_bounds=(R_lo,R_hi)` labels a band of complete flux surfaces.
It does not give the rectangular file's R bounds or crop the equilibrium.
It requests adequate physical coverage and reports corresponding r, psi, and
normalized flux radii. With it, cover the larger of its outer surface and the
LCFS, plus a guard. Without it, cover the LCFS plus a guard. Enlarging the R–Z
rectangle alone does not certify additional physical coverage.

CLI: input filename; `--output` (default input stem plus `.geqdsk`);
`--nr`/`--nz` (257 each); `--rtol` (1e-10); `--rz-bounds RMIN RMAX ZMIN ZMAX`;
`--guard-fraction` (0.05); and `--plot FILE`. Use odd mesh dimensions, at least
five nodes. There is no command-line expression parser for q.

### Geometry and numerical methods

Use

\[
R=R_{axis}-a_{shift}r^2/(2R_{axis})
  +r\cos[\theta+\arcsin(\delta)\sin\theta],\qquad
Z=Z_{axis}+\kappa r\sin\theta.
\]

Implement analytic derivatives and
\(J_r=R(R_rZ_\theta-R_\theta Z_r)\). Set
\(F=R_{axis}B_{axis}\), \(B_\phi=F/R\), and

\[
\psi'(r)=\frac{F}{2\pi q(R_{omp}(r))}
\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{J_r}{R^2}\,d\theta,\qquad
R_{omp}(r)=R_{axis}-a_{shift}r^2/(2R_{axis})+r.
\]

Set axis flux to zero, invert `R_lcfs` for the LCFS radius a, and use psi(a)
as boundary flux. Provide stable coordinate conversions, including the zero
shift limit and rho=sqrt(psi/psi_boundary), allowing rho>1 in the valid region.
Initially require positive B_axis and finite positive q, outward increasing
psi, positive R, and nested surfaces. Negative triangularity and either sign
of magnetic shear are supported. q must cover the axis through the guard.

Separate geometry evaluation, radial flux construction, rectangular sampling,
and serialization. Use s=r^2 for radial tabulation, adaptive poloidal quadrature,
and the finite axis limit of dpsi/ds. Integrate a shape-preserving interpolant of
dpsi/ds, refine against independent midpoint values, and invert flux by bracketed
root finding. Use scaled absolute as well as relative tolerances.

Invert the analytic R–Z mapping directly. With v=(Z-Z_axis)/kappa and
u=r cos(theta), r=sqrt(u^2+v^2), solve the scalar R(u,v) equation on the branch
connected to the axis. Safeguard and verify inversion; report failures by point.

Place the guard beyond the outer required surface. Derive a padded R–Z rectangle
from the guard contour, with RMIN>0, unless bounds are explicitly supplied.
For corners outside the physical region, use the specified continuation
psi(s)=psi(s_guard)+psi_s(s_guard)*(s-s_guard). It matches flux and its first
derivative and is increasing. Do not evaluate physical q integrals there.
Identify this background region in plots and metadata. Keep certified contours
and LCFS at least three R–Z cells away from the continuation interface and box
boundary; reject insufficient coverage with corrective guidance.

### Output and device examples

Write standard fixed-width GEQDSK, including partial final records, R-fastest
PSIRZ, constant FPOL, zero FFPRIM, QPSI on uniform axis-to-LCFS flux nodes, and
interleaved LCFS coordinate pairs. Use LIMITR=0. Pressure, its derivative, and
current are zero placeholders, documented as such. Use a deterministic header.
Validate numerical data before replacing output.

Write a JSON companion with inputs and source hash, numerical settings, flux
metadata, physical/guard/rectangle bounds, conversion table, and residuals.
Optional plots show contours, LCFS, coverage, guard, continuation, q, and psi(r).

Preserve DIII-D and TCV field and shape parameters and q polynomials. For TCV,
use reflect=false and derive exact example bounds from the existing r(x)
mapping: approximately (1.051359,1.155593) m, rather than nominal Rmid bounds.
Nonzero shift means dR_omp/dr=1-a_shift*r/R_axis; x increments in that input
are Miller-radius increments.

For LTX, replace the old rational profile (pole at R_omp approximately
0.688328 m) with
q(r)=q_LCFS*exp[shat_LCFS/2*((r/a)^2-1)]. This is positive, regular at the axis,
and preserves both LCFS q and shear. Document the intentional difference.

### Documentation and acceptance

The LaTeX source documents coordinates, units, derivatives, Jacobian, magnetic
field, q–psi relation, inversions, axis limits, quadrature, interpolation,
coverage, continuation, error controls, file ordering, placeholders, examples,
and verification results. Compile when a LaTeX installation is available.

Use Python unittest and the repository's C framework. Test derivatives,
round trips, both signs of triangularity, shift and vertical offset, file ordering,
non-square grids, partial records, CLI errors, invalid q and geometry, and all
three simulation-domain arrangements. Test both omitted coverage and explicit
R–Z bounds. Independently refine radial and rectangular discretizations.

For circular constant-q surfaces use the independent reference
psi(r)=F/q*(R_axis-sqrt(R_axis^2-r^2)). Target normalized analytic/conversion
errors <=1e-8. Test R–Z meshes 65,129,257, extending to 513 as necessary;
reconstructed B, Bp, and contour-derived q must agree within 1e-3 on the
requested device regions at the accepted resolution. Require convergent
surface locations, no extra X-points/broken contours in the certified region,
and successful tokamak geometry construction for all three devices. Compare
physical quantities before metrics, which require coordinate transformations.
Full turbulence runs are not required for Stage 1.

## Stage 2: C updater

Implement `gyrokinetic/zero/gen_miller_eqdsk.c`, public
`gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.h`, and `ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk.c`. Accept scalar geometry
and a q callback/context with the same R_omp convention. Provide initialization,
generation/evaluation, writing, release, flux metadata, and conversions.
Run on CPU during initialization. Keep MPI/app policy outside the updater;
reuse Gkeyll numerical utilities where accurate enough. Test analytic and
Python references, reader compatibility, invalid inputs, lifecycle, and memory.
Finalize exact signatures after Stage 1 validation.

## Stage 3: App integration

Append GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER without changing existing enum values; add public
Miller geometry inputs. Initially specify simulation bounds by R_omp.
Calculate conversions before constructing the configuration grid, generate the
file on rank zero, communicate failures and synchronize readers, populate EFIT
and tokamak inputs, and resolve effective type to GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK before
downstream geometry/species initialization.

Distinguish equilibrium LCFS metadata from an internal computational split.
Core annuli need closed-line BCs, SOL-only domains need IWL open-line BCs,
and crossing domains need a split at a cell boundary. Reject incompatible
bounds/cells without moving surfaces silently. Migrate source and initial
profiles, binormal normalization, and parallel coordinates as needed to preserve
physical meaning in DIII-D/TCV comparisons.

Test serial initialization and a short step, then MPI/GPU smoke tests where
available. Preserve the generated file, resolved bounds, and provenance.
Specify multiblock, restart reuse, and language bindings when Stage 3 begins.

---
name: code_style
description: Gkeyll's C/C++/CUDA code style is enforced by clang-format. Use when writing or editing any .c/.h/.cpp/.hpp/.cu/.cuh file, to know how to format it and which files must never be reformatted. Also use when writing or editing python scripts.
user-invocable: true
---

# Instructions

* Operate relative to the repo root (detect via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

# Code style

The style itself (indentation, brace placement, spacing, etc.) is defined by the
root `.clang-format` file plus one rule in `ci/format.py` (designated-initializer
layout, see below). Don't try to memorize or restate those rules -- just run the
formatter and let it decide:

```
python3 ci/format.py <file>...
```

Do not run bare `clang-format -i`: it packs designated initializers back onto one
line. `ci/format.py` needs clang-format 18.1.8 on PATH (`pip install clang-format==18.1.8`).

A `pre-commit` hook runs this automatically on commit, and CI (`.github/workflows/format-check.yml`)
double-checks on push/PR, so a file that hasn't been run through clang-format will
get reformatted or flagged regardless.

## The rules the config file can't express: never format `ker/` or `core/minus/`

Two kinds of files must never be run through clang-format, and never hand-formatted
to "match" the style either -- leave them exactly as they are:

- Any path matching `*/ker/*` (e.g. `core/ker/`, `gyrokinetic/ker/`) contains
  auto-generated DG kernel code (see `gkeyll_guide`'s note on `ker/`: generated with
  Maxima, never hand-edited).
- Anything under `core/minus/` is a vendored third-party library (e.g. sqlite3,
  kann, pcg_basic, STC), not Gkeyll's own code.

    bounds = np.asarray(rz_bounds, dtype=float)
    if bounds.shape != (4,) or not np.all(np.isfinite(bounds)):

    rmin, rmax, zmin, zmax = bounds
    if not (0 < rmin < g.R_axis < rmax and zmin < g.Z_axis < zmax):
        raise ValueError("R–Z bounds must have RMIN>0 and contain the magnetic axis")
    Rgrid, Zgrid = np.linspace(rmin, rmax, nr), np.linspace(zmin, zmax, nz)
    spacing = np.array([(rmax-rmin)/(nr-1), (zmax-zmin)/(nz-1)])
    guard_tree = cKDTree(np.column_stack((Rg, Zg))/spacing)
    clearance = math.inf
    for radius in (eq.a, eq.r_required):

def _write_values(stream, values):
    array = np.asarray(values).ravel()
    for first in range(0, len(array), 5):
        fields = [f"{float(value):16.9E}" for value in array[first:first+5]]
        if any(len(field) != 16 for field in fields):
            raise ValueError("value exceeds GEQDSK E16.9 width")
        stream.write("".join(fields)+"\n")


def _atomic_text(path, writer):
    """Write in the destination directory and replace only after successful close."""
    path = Path(path)
    temporary = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", encoding="ascii", newline="\n",
                                         dir=path.parent, prefix=f".{path.name}.", delete=False) as stream:
            temporary = Path(stream.name)
            writer(stream)
        temporary.replace(path)

            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def write_eqdsk(filename, equilibrium, sampled):
    """Write a deterministic GEQDSK with explicit zero pressure/current placeholders."""
    eq, g = equilibrium, equilibrium.geometry
    R, Z = sampled["R"], sampled["Z"]
    nr, nz = len(R), len(Z)

    def write(stream):
        stream.write(f"{'GKEYLL SYNTHETIC MILLER':48s}{0:4d}{nr:4d}{nz:4d}\n")
        _write_values(stream, [R[-1]-R[0], Z[-1]-Z[0], g.R_axis, R[0], (Z[0]+Z[-1])/2])
        _write_values(stream, [g.R_axis, g.Z_axis, 0, eq.psi_boundary, g.B_axis])
        _write_values(stream, [0, 0, 0, g.R_axis, 0])
        _write_values(stream, [g.Z_axis, 0, eq.psi_boundary, 0, 0])

            _write_values(stream, profile)

        _write_values(stream, sampled["qpsi"])
        stream.write(f"{len(sampled['boundary']):5d}{0:5d}\n")

                         "radial_relative_error": eq.radial_error,

            "exterior_nodes": int(np.count_nonzero(sampled["exterior"])),
            "conventions": {"psi": "poloidal flux / (2*pi), increasing outwards; axis=0",
                            "q_argument": "outboard midplane major radius [m]",
                            "exterior": "linear in r^2 beyond guard; not physical coverage",
                            "pressure_and_current": "zero placeholders; not a Grad-Shafranov solution",

{"chunk_id":"6564b9","wall_time_seconds":0.043312167,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":2178,"output":"Collection of sample GEQDSK files

Miller generator
================

gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py is both an importable module and a command-line
generator. It requires NumPy and SciPy. Matplotlib is optional, for --plot.
The implementation plan is MILLER_EQDSK_PLAN.md; all formulas and numerical
methods are documented in gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex.

From the repository root:

  python3 gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py \
    gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/miller_tcv.py --output tcv_miller.geqdsk \
    --nr 257 --nz 257 --plot tcv_miller.png

The Python input defines geometry={...} and a scalar q(R_omp) function. All
physical parameters belong in that file; the CLI never evaluates a function
expression. R_omp is outboard midplane MAJOR radius in meters. Required geometry
keys are R_axis, B_axis (toroidal field), and R_lcfs (outboard LCFS major radius).
Defaults: Z_axis=0, kappa=1, delta=0, a_shift=0. Lengths are meters and fields
tesla. The initial convention requires positive B_axis and positive finite q.

Optional R_omp_bounds=(lower,upper) requests coverage of complete flux surfaces
for a core annulus, SOL-only simulation, or LCFS-crossing simulation. These are
NOT rectangular R bounds. The equilibrium always includes the axis and LCFS;
q must be valid all the way from the axis through the physical guard surface.
Without coverage bounds the LCFS is the outer certified surface. --rz-bounds
RMIN RMAX ZMIN ZMAX explicitly sets the rectangular grid but does not extend
the certified physical surfaces. Rectangular corners use the documented smooth
flux continuation beyond the guard, identified in the JSON summary and plots.
The default 5-percent guard needs at least three R-Z cells of clearance; coarse
grids may require --guard-fraction 0.25. The node counts must be odd, 5..999.

The output includes <output>.json, with parameters, input provenance, flux
values, physical coverage, a conversion table, and numerical residuals. The
GEQDSK has constant F=R_axis*B_axis and zero pressure/current placeholders. It is
a synthetic magnetic geometry, not a Grad-Shafranov solution or a wall model.
No limiter is written. The existing tokamak IWL machinery supplies wall cuts.

Examples miller_d3d.py and miller_tcv.py preserve their corresponding analytic
regression inputs' surfaces and q profiles. TCV uses the actual shifted r(x)
endpoint surfaces, not its nominal Rmid bounds. Read it with reflect=false to
preserve Z_axis. LTX replaces the old rational q profile (pole at R_omp about
0.688328 m) with a positive exponential profile preserving LCFS q and shear.
The original script and data file remain available for comparison.

Python API:

  from gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk import (
      MillerGeometry, MillerEquilibrium, sample_eqdsk, write_eqdsk)
  geometry = MillerGeometry(R_axis=2, B_axis=1.5, R_lcfs=2.5)
  equilibrium = MillerEquilibrium(geometry, lambda R_omp: 2)
  data = sample_eqdsk(equilibrium)
  write_eqdsk("circle.geqdsk", equilibrium, data)
  print(equilibrium.coordinates(2.4))  # R_omp, Miller r, psi, rho_psi, q.

Verification:

  python3 -m unittest discover -s gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk -v
  make -j6 LIBRARY_TARGET=library gyrokinetic
  make -j6 build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk
  ./build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk

Use no more than half the available processors for make. To exercise the native
reader on Python outputs as well, generate files named miller_ltx.geqdsk,
miller_d3d.geqdsk, and miller_tcv.geqdsk in one directory, then run the same C
test with GKYL_MILLER_REFERENCE_DIR set to that directory. Native tests always
construct their own temporary fixtures, so normal unit runs need no Python.
Both quadratic and cubic reconstructions are checked; full geometry creation
uses the existing quadratic tokamak path. LaTeX can be checked with:

  pdflatex -halt-on-error -output-directory=/tmp \
    gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex

Native updater and app API
=========================

gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.h exposes _inew, _advance, _write, _get_info,
_psi_from_omp, _omp_from_psi, _surface, and _release. Its qprofile callback takes
(double R_omp, void *ctx). The native angular quadrature uses periodic
trapezoidal refinement with an explicit convergence test; radial interpolation
and the rectangular continuation follow the Python reference. It is a host
initialization updater, with no CUDA or MPI dependency.

The app accepts geometry.geometry_id=GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER and parameters in
geometry.miller_grid_info, of type struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inp. In this mode
app lower[0] and upper[0] are outboard major radii. Initialization resolves the
mutable input IN PLACE to psi bounds and GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK, before creating
the configuration grid. Solver callbacks therefore receive the ordinary
tokamak coordinates (psi, alpha, parallel coordinate). They do not receive the
old analytic input's (x,y,theta). Use the updater conversions when migrating
physical profiles. Binormal extents and parallel coordinates use the existing
tokamak conventions; arbitrary analytic-input callbacks cannot be reused
without their coordinate transformations.

Generation writes <app-name>-miller.geqdsk unless geometry.efit_info.filepath is
set. Rank zero writes, collective status handling precedes reading, and the
file is retained. Generation parameters are recorded in geometry metadata.
The q callback must be deterministic and identical on all ranks. Initialization
regenerates the file, including before a restart; there is no cached-file reuse
mode. Keep the same geometry and q inputs when restarting a simulation.
The app selects IWL geometry, disables reflection, and derives R-Z search bounds.
It supports single-block 2x/3x domains, excluding the coordinate singularity at
the magnetic axis. Multiblock and language-binding APIs are not provided here.

An LCFS crossing sets has_LCFS and must align with a psi cell face. No requested
domain surfaces are moved; mismatch beyond GEQDSK serialization precision
causes initialization to fail. x_LCFS is represented by the matching grid face;
the wall cutoff uses the serialized boundary flux. Core-only and SOL-only
domains have no internal split. Set ordinary species BCs: twist-shift for a
3x core annulus, and the desired open-line BCs for SOL/crossing cases. The app's
existing mixed-domain machinery handles the core part of a crossing.

The focused regression rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 constructs all three domains and
advances each by one step. It uses constant profiles and a static zero field
to isolate geometry/BC initialization. Run in a scratch directory to contain
its output; MPI partitions the parallel (third configuration) direction:

  make -j6 build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1
  ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 -s1
  <MPI-prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 2 \
    ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_miller_3x2v_p1 -M -e2 -s1

Check the returned app pointer for NULL after a Miller initialization failure.

Put the geqdsk file you want in this folder and name it 'input.geqdsk' in order to run g0 unit tests with it

File descriptions:

- asdex.geqdsk: Similar to what was used in D. Michels, et al. Phys. Plasmas
  29, 032307 (2022).
- cerfon.geqdsk: Generated from analytical equilibrium in Antoine J. Cerfon and Jeffrey P. Freidberg, PHYSICS OF PLASMAS 17, 032502 (2010)
- elliptical.geqdsk: Fake equilibriuum generated using elliptical flux surfaces
- nstxu_DN.geqdsk: Double-null equilibrium (with lowest drsep value) from NSTX-U test run in March 2016 . Original file name on PPPL Flux cluster: g203655.00304 (shot number = 203655, time-stamp = 304 ms).
- nstxu_SN.geqdsk: Single-null equilibrium from NSTX-U test run in April 2016. Original file name on PPPL Flux cluster: g204700.00238 (shot number = 204700, time-stamp = 238 ms).
- solovev.geqdsk: Generated from analytical equilibrium described in Noah Mandell's thesis Sec. 5.3
- step.geqdsk: From STEP. Proposed magnetic equilibrium.
- wham.geqdsk: case with beams and ~0.8 T central field.
- tcv.geqdsk:  TCV equilibrium from Oliveira and Body et. al., Nuclear Fusion, 2021. https://github.com/SPCData/TCV-X21/blob/main/1.experimental_data/reference_scenario/65402_t1.eqdsk
- tcv_upper_SN.geqdsk: TCV upper single null equilibrium g162940.02944_670 from Gabriele Merlo and David Hatch
- mast.geadsk: generated with the tutorial from freegs

# Sample GEQDSK files

## Miller generator

[gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py](gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py) is both an importable module and a command-line
generator. It requires NumPy and SciPy. Matplotlib is optional, for `--plot`.
The implementation plan is [MILLER_EQDSK_PLAN.md](MILLER_EQDSK_PLAN.md); all formulas and numerical
methods are documented in [gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex](gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex).

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.py \
  gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/miller_tcv.py --output tcv_miller.geqdsk \
  --nr 257 --nz 257 --plot tcv_miller.png
```

The Python input defines `geometry={...}` and a scalar `q(R_omp)` function. All
physical parameters belong in that file; the CLI never evaluates a function
expression. `R_omp` is outboard midplane MAJOR radius in meters. Required geometry
keys are `R_axis`, `B_axis` (toroidal field), and `R_lcfs` (outboard LCFS major radius).
Defaults: `Z_axis=0`, `kappa=1`, `delta=0`, `a_shift=0`. Lengths are meters and fields
tesla. The initial convention requires positive `B_axis` and positive finite q.

Optional `R_omp_bounds=(lower,upper)` requests coverage of complete flux surfaces
for a core annulus, SOL-only simulation, or LCFS-crossing simulation. These are
NOT rectangular R bounds. The equilibrium always includes the axis and LCFS;
q must be valid all the way from the axis through the physical guard surface.
Without coverage bounds the LCFS is the outer certified surface. `--rz-bounds RMIN RMAX ZMIN ZMAX` explicitly sets the rectangular grid but does not extend
the certified physical surfaces. Rectangular corners use the documented smooth
flux continuation beyond the guard, identified in the JSON summary and plots.
The default 5-percent guard needs at least three R-Z cells of clearance; coarse
grids may require `--guard-fraction 0.25`. The node counts must be odd, 5..999.

The output includes `<output>.json`, with parameters, input provenance, flux
values, physical coverage, a conversion table, and numerical residuals. The
GEQDSK has constant `F=R_axis*B_axis` and zero pressure/current placeholders. It is
a synthetic magnetic geometry, not a Grad-Shafranov solution or a wall model.
No limiter is written. The existing tokamak IWL machinery supplies wall cuts.

Examples [miller_d3d.py](miller_d3d.py) and [miller_tcv.py](miller_tcv.py) preserve their corresponding analytic
regression inputs' surfaces and q profiles. TCV uses the actual shifted `r(x)`
endpoint surfaces, not its nominal `Rmid` bounds. Read it with `reflect=false` to
preserve `Z_axis`. LTX replaces the old rational q profile (pole at `R_omp` about
0.688328 m) with a positive exponential profile preserving LCFS q and shear.
The original script and data file remain available for comparison.

### Python API

```python
from gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk import (
    MillerGeometry, MillerEquilibrium, sample_eqdsk, write_eqdsk)
geometry = MillerGeometry(R_axis=2, B_axis=1.5, R_lcfs=2.5)
equilibrium = MillerEquilibrium(geometry, lambda R_omp: 2)
data = sample_eqdsk(equilibrium)
write_eqdsk("circle.geqdsk", equilibrium, data)
print(equilibrium.coordinates(2.4))  # R_omp, Miller r, psi, rho_psi, q.
```

### Verification

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk -v
make -j6 LIBRARY_TARGET=library gyrokinetic
make -j6 build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk
./build/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_gen_miller_eqdsk
```

Use no more than half the available processors for make. To exercise the native
reader on Python outputs as well, generate files named miller_ltx.geqdsk,
miller_d3d.geqdsk, and miller_tcv.geqdsk in one directory, then run the same C
test with `GKYL_MILLER_REFERENCE_DIR` set to that directory. Native tests always
construct their own temporary fixtures, so normal unit runs need no Python.
Both quadratic and cubic reconstructions are checked; full geometry creation
uses the existing quadratic tokamak path. LaTeX can be checked with:

```bash
pdflatex -halt-on-error -output-directory=/tmp \
  gyrokinetic/data/eqdsk/gkeyll_gen_miller_eqdsk.tex
```

## Native updater and app API

[gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.h](../../zero/gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk.h) exposes `_inew`, `_advance`, `_write`, `_get_info`,
`_psi_from_omp`, `_omp_from_psi`, `_surface`, and `_release`. Its `qprofile` callback takes
`(double R_omp, void *ctx)`. The native angular quadrature uses periodic
trapezoidal refinement with an explicit convergence test; radial interpolation
and the rectangular continuation follow the Python reference. It is a host
initialization updater, with no CUDA or MPI dependency.

The app accepts `geometry.geometry_id=GKYL_GEOMETRY_MILLER` and parameters in
`geometry.miller_grid_info`, of type `struct gkyl_gen_miller_eqdsk_inp`. In this mode
app `lower[0]` and `upper[0]` are outboard major radii. Initialization resolves the
mutable input IN PLACE to psi bounds and `GKYL_GEOMETRY_TOKAMAK`, before creating
the configuration grid. Solver callbacks therefore receive the ordinary
tokamak coordinates (psi, alpha, parallel coordinate). They do not receive the
old analytic input's (x,y,theta). Use the updater conversions when migrating
physical profiles. Binormal extents and parallel coordinates use the existing
tokamak conventions; arbitrary analytic-input callbacks cannot be reused
without their coordinate transformations.

    sampled = sample_eqdsk(eq, args.nr, args.nz, args.rz_bounds)
    metadata = summary(eq, sampled, source)
    write_eqdsk(output, eq, sampled)
    _atomic_text(str(output)+".json", lambda stream: json.dump(metadata, stream, indent=2, allow_nan=False))
    if args.plot:

    return 1

name: code_style
description: Gkeyll's C/C++/CUDA code style is enforced by clang-format. Use when writing or editing any .c/.h/.cpp/.hpp/.cu/.cuh file, to know how to format it and which files must never be reformatted. Also use when writing or editing python scripts.
user-invocable: true

# Instructions

* Operate relative to the repo root (detect via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

# Code style

The style itself (indentation, brace placement, spacing, etc.) is defined by the
root `.clang-format` file plus one rule in `ci/format.py` (designated-initializer
layout, see below). Don't try to memorize or restate those rules -- just run the
formatter and let it decide:

```
python3 ci/format.py <file>...
```

Do not run bare `clang-format -i`: it packs designated initializers back onto one
line. `ci/format.py` needs clang-format 18.1.8 on PATH (`pip install clang-format==18.1.8`).

A `pre-commit` hook runs this automatically on commit, and CI (`.github/workflows/format-check.yml`)
double-checks on push/PR, so a file that hasn't been run through clang-format will
get reformatted or flagged regardless.

## The rules the config file can't express: never format `ker/` or `core/minus/`

Two kinds of files must never be run through clang-format, and never hand-formatted
to "match" the style either -- leave them exactly as they are:

- Any path matching `*/ker/*` (e.g. `core/ker/`, `gyrokinetic/ker/`) contains
  auto-generated DG kernel code (see `gkeyll_guide`'s note on `ker/`: generated with
  Maxima, never hand-edited).
- Anything under `core/minus/` is a vendored third-party library (e.g. sqlite3,
  kann, pcg_basic, STC), not Gkeyll's own code.

The pre-commit hook and CI already exclude both for this reason.

## Designated initializers: the script decides, not the trailing comma

A designated initializer that fits on one line stays on one line. One that does
not gets one member per line, first member below the `{`, closing `}` on its own
line. `ci/format.py` enforces this by stripping every trailing comma, running
clang-format, re-adding a trailing comma to each list that did not fit, and running
clang-format again. So don't add or remove trailing commas to steer the layout;
write the list any way you like and run the script.

## Two conventions the formatter enforces that you should know when reading code

- Every function *definition* has its return type on its own line, so
  `grep '^gkyl_foo('` finds the definition. Declarations keep the type on the same line.
- `case` labels are indented one level inside `switch`.

# Python style

Use the following style rules to format Python.

- Use 2-spaces instead of indents, 4-spaces, or 4-space indents.

The style itself (indentation, brace placement, spacing, etc.) is defined by the
root `.clang-format` file plus one rule in `ci/format.py` (designated-initializer
layout, see below). Don't try to memorize or restate those rules -- just run the

```

```

line. `ci/format.py` needs clang-format 18.1.8 on PATH (`pip install clang-format==18.1.8`).

A `pre-commit` hook runs this automatically on commit, and CI (`.github/workflows/format-check.yml`)
double-checks on push/PR, so a file that hasn't been run through clang-format will
get reformatted or flagged regardless.

not gets one member per line, first member below the `{`, closing `}` on its own
line. `ci/format.py` enforces this by stripping every trailing comma, running
clang-format, re-adding a trailing comma to each list that did not fit, and running
clang-format again. So don't add or remove trailing commas to steer the layout;
write the list any way you like and run the script.

  `grep '^gkyl_foo('` finds the definition. Declarations keep the type on the same line.

Use the following style rules to format Python.

- Use 2-spaces instead of indents, 4-spaces, or 4-space indents.
